summary: Sequencing hold, not a rejection of the design. The stage-3 kernel this builds on never ran in the timed call. It failed its own self-check (case 2: B=6, kv_scale 0.25, grid 3, rel L2 1.23 for both ticket and B8), so 1.380x is master's paired FA3 re-measured. This stage needs the regime that failed (several tiles per CTA, at batch 16/32), and its self-check covers batch 16/32, so it would fall back too and measure nothing. Fix stage 3's multi-tile bug first (as stage 4), then re-mint this as stage 5.
justification: Parent evidence (archive/full-verify-wgmma-s3-warpgroup-per-kvhead-inproc/2c3f7fff72bb4e1d.log). The sm_90a build was good: 128 regs, 0 local bytes, binaryVersion 90, 2 CTAs/SM, 91.7 KB smem. The ticket canary ([70,13], grid 4) passed, and so did case 1 (lens_a, kv_scale 1.0, grid 264), at 4.8e-3. Case 2 (lens_a, kv_scale 0.25, grid 3) returned rel L2 1.23 for both the ticket and the B8 variants, and the log then shows 'PATH CHOSEN: full verify master FA3, paired heads (fallback ...)'. The attribution table agrees: full verify_16 162.61 us and verify_32 301.91 us equal master's incumbent (162.7/301.3), and those 'gains' are only against the stage-2 base. The wgmma kernel has no timing anywhere, so M2/M3 have no evidence behind them. What the passing cases did NOT exercise: lens_a has 242 tiles at grid 264, and the canary has 3 tiles at grid 4, so every passing launch gave each CTA at most 1 tile. Case 2 is the first launch with about 81 tiles per CTA. That covers ring wrap-around and mbarrier phase parity, the double-buffered V^T reuse, segments that cross request boundaries (Q reload), and page-index block rotation past IDX_TILES=16. B8 fails identically, so the fault is in the main kernel, not the ticket merge. Case 2 also changed kv_scale to 0.25, so the cause is confounded between multi-tile and scale, but rel L2 1.23 looks like garbage, not a scale error (a missing or doubled 0.25 gives about 0.75/0.94/3). How this lands on the target shapes: sliding verify_1 has about 33 tiles with grid 33, so 1 tile per CTA, which is the regime that passed. verify_16 (528 tiles, grid 264) and verify_32 (1056 tiles) need 2 and 4 tiles per CTA, which is the regime that failed. The specified self-check includes batch 16/32 and turns off the whole sliding route on any failure, so the run would almost certainly print 'sliding verify FA3 (fallback)' and re-measure master. Design on its own merits: the incumbent numbers (16.7/22.7/28.7 us; FA3 main 7.6/10.7/14.5 + combine 3.9/4.1/4.3 + prepare 1.7) match FINDINGS. The floors are tiny (0.1/1.9/3.7), so the shapes are latency- and launch-bound, and folding prepare + combine + norm-gate into one launch is the right lever. The windowed key range [lo_b, seq_b) with in-kernel lo_b, plus the extra lower-edge mask, correctly reproduces FA3 window_size=(window-1, 0). WEAKEST LINK, even after the fix: at verify_1 the ticket's last CTA LSE-merges 33 partials of 8x16x64 fp32 (32 KB each, about 1 MB) by itself. One SM streams that at roughly 0.1-0.2 TB/s, so 5-10 us of serial tail, which alone threatens M2 (<= 13 us) and rules out M3 (<= 10 us). The batch-1 sibling solves the same problem with a two-level merge. Here the cheaper fix is fewer, longer segments at batch 1 (e.g. grid 8-11, 3-4 tiles each), but that again needs the broken multi-tile path. Expected directions are consistent with TASK.md (sliding verify weight 46 per load). The 'full flat' expectation holds only because full verify is on the fallback.
confounders: full-verify-wgmma-s3-warpgroup-per-kvhead-inproc (parent, not landed): its kernel failed self-check and never ran, so this stage would build on unmeasured and incorrect code. Any result would be read against a parent with no timing.

sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv / sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: these own sliding decode only and are untouched. Sliding decode stays on master code, and the predicate's q_len 8 keeps them out, so they do not confound.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing + paired-heads-launch-cleanup: sliding verify is unpaired on master (PAIRED=False), so routing it to the new kernel changes no pre-attention layout. Full verify_16/32 stay on the paired FA3 fallback while the stage-3 kernel is broken, so 'full flat' is master's code, not stage 3's.
fused-preattention-triton: provides the e4m3 q in the unpaired [B*8,16,64] layout that the A operand reads. That layout is the same as for full verify, so it does not confound.
interference: No companion would help: the problem is not attribution but that the measured path would be the fallback. The right follow-up is a correctness stage on the parent: 'full-verify-wgmma-s4-multitile-fix', built on the stage-3 branch. Its self-check should separate case 2 into (lens_a, 1.0, grid 3), (lens_a, 0.25, grid 264), and single-request multi-tile cases with N = 2, 4 and 17 tiles per CTA, printing per-case rel L2 and the device error word (wait timeouts set it). That locates the fault (multi-tile ring/phase, V^T reuse, request crossing, meta rotation, or kv_scale) in one okc check. Once stage 3 passes and is timed on full verify_16/32, re-mint this as the next stage. Add a batch-1 segment-length choice (grid of about 8-11 at sliding verify_1) or a two-level merge, so the single-CTA 1 MB merge does not dominate.
rules_flags: None blocking in the design. The window predicate and grid come from config only; lo_b is computed in-kernel from cache_seqlens, every key in each window is attended, and the self-check runs in-process at import (no subprocess).

The workspace and ticket buffer are zero buffers allocated at import, not derived from inputs, so they are allowed. If both full and sliding routes use the ticket kernel in one step, they need separate ticket arrays (or a strict reset-before-reuse guarantee) so that a sliding launch never sees a full launch's non-zero ticket.
open_questions: Which variable broke case 2: about 81 tiles per CTA (ring phase / V^T double buffer / request crossing / IDX_TILES rotation) or kv_scale 0.25? Every passing launch had at most 1 tile per CTA.
Did the device error word (bounded mbarrier wait timeout) get set in case 2? The log does not print it.
At sliding verify_1, what does the single-CTA merge of 33 x 32 KB partials cost? Stamp it with clock64 in the self-check before committing to grid = Ttot.

If the orchestrator would rather not add a stage: proceed only if the implementer first reproduces and fixes case 2 on this branch and the self-check passes at batch 16/32. Otherwise retire this run before it spends a check.
